answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable deposit that is slashed when the same behaviour echoes across several accounts: a hollow credential with no stake behind it buys no trust, so an attacker pays per copy and forfeits everything once the overlap is proven. The failure mode is a wealthy sybil simply buying many deposits, so the deposit must grow steeply with each extra identity funded from the same source. Check it by tracing deposit origins on the ledger and flagging clusters that fan out from one knoll of funds.
